name: SpeedSearch
author: TMM Technology

sections.description:
Help shoppers find the right product faster.

A growing catalogue should give customers more choice without making products harder to find. SpeedSearch brings dedicated product search, autocomplete and flexible filtering to WooCommerce, helping shoppers move from a search or a category to the products that fit.

Search and filtering run on the SpeedSearch backend, reducing the search workload on your WordPress database. Your store gets a product-discovery interface you can configure in WordPress, with background catalogue synchronization to keep it supplied with updates.

Give shoppers more ways to find what they want

  • Search with a head start. Show suggestions and product results as customers type.
  • Turn a large selection into a useful shortlist. Filter by category, tag, price and product attributes such as size, colour or material.
  • Put discovery where it belongs. Place a complete search interface or individual search, filter and results components in your storefront.
  • Keep catalogue changes moving. Synchronize product and taxonomy updates through background processing, with diagnostics to inspect progress.

Give WooCommerce search its own engine

Search and filtering can ask a lot of a store’s database, particularly as its catalogue and filter combinations grow. SpeedSearch synchronizes catalogue data with a dedicated service that finds matching products and processes filters.

This separates those operations from your store’s main WordPress database. It is designed to improve product discovery; actual speed depends on your catalogue, hosting, network, theme and configuration.

Help both focused shoppers and browsers

Some customers arrive with a product in mind. Others start with a category, a budget or a preferred colour. Autocomplete supports the first group; product filters help the second narrow down the options.

Configure the autocomplete presentation and selection behaviour, then choose filters that reflect how people shop your catalogue. Attribute filters use the supported attributes configured on your WooCommerce products.

Fit search into your storefront

Use shortcodes for the full interface or for individual search, filter, category and product-results components. SpeedSearch also includes integrations for Flatsome and its UX Builder.

Adjust the layout and behaviour in WordPress, then check the result with your theme and product templates. You can build around the way your shop presents its products.

See what shoppers are searching for

Search analytics can help you review popular search terms and searches without results. Use those insights to investigate gaps in product naming, catalogue coverage or navigation.

Connect your catalogue and get started

SpeedSearch requires access to the SpeedSearch backend service, store authorization and an initial catalogue synchronization. Installing the plugin alone does not provide service access.

Visit SpeedSearch to learn about the service, review the available plans, or contact wp@tmm.ventures for setup assistance. Paid plans are separate from the plugin download.

External Services

SpeedSearch backend

The plugin connects to the SpeedSearch service to authorize the store, synchronize its catalogue and settings, and process search, autocomplete and filtering requests. The default backend address is https://saffy.speedsearchpro.com; deployments can configure a different address.

Data exchanged includes product and taxonomy information, store settings, search and filter parameters, the store domain, plugin version and service authentication details. During authorization, the plugin also sends the activating administrator’s name and email address as the store contact. Background analytics delivery sends per-product view, add-to-cart and purchase counters.

These requests occur during store connection, catalogue and settings synchronization, search operations and scheduled analytics delivery. Diagnostic and settings-sharing operations also communicate with the backend when used.

Service information: https://speedsearch.io/
For service access, terms and privacy information, contact wp@tmm.ventures.

Tawk.to live chat

SpeedSearch loads Tawk.to’s chat widget in its administration interface to provide support. Loading the widget connects the administrator’s browser to Tawk.to, exposing connection information such as the IP address and browser details. Information entered into the chat is sent to Tawk.to.

Privacy policy | Terms of service
sections.installation:
Requirements

  • WordPress with WooCommerce installed and activated.
  • PHP 8.1 or newer, with curl, dom, json, libxml and mbstring.
  • Access to the SpeedSearch backend service.
  • Working WordPress background processing for catalogue synchronization.

Set up your first product search

  1. Install and activate SpeedSearch alongside WooCommerce. Use a staging copy to check your theme integration first.
  2. Open the SpeedSearch administration pages and connect and authorize your store. Contact support if you need service access.
  3. Allow the initial catalogue synchronization to complete.
  4. Choose the search interface and filters that suit your catalogue.
  5. Add the interface using the available shortcodes or supported theme integration.
  6. Search for a known product, combine a few filters and follow a product link. Check the experience on desktop and mobile before enabling it for customers.

If products do not appear, check the service connection, synchronization diagnostics and scheduled background tasks.

Screenshots show example catalogues and an earlier interface; appearance and available controls depend on the theme, settings and version.
sections.faq:
How does SpeedSearch help speed up WooCommerce?

SpeedSearch uses a dedicated backend to find matching products and process filters, reducing reliance on WordPress database queries for those operations. The improvement depends on your store and configuration.

SpeedSearch focuses on product discovery. It does not optimize unrelated checkout, payment or administration operations.

Does SpeedSearch work without an external service?

No. Backend-powered search and filtering require a connection to the SpeedSearch service, store authorization and a synchronized catalogue. Installing the plugin alone does not provide service access.

Can I filter products by colour, size or material?

Yes, when those values are configured as supported WooCommerce product attributes. You can also use category, tag and price filters.

Does it include autocomplete?

Yes. SpeedSearch can display suggestions as customers type, with settings for autocomplete presentation and behaviour.

Can I choose where the search field and filters appear?

Yes. Use the complete interface or individual shortcode components. The plugin also includes Flatsome and UX Builder integrations.

Will it work with my theme?

Compatibility depends on your theme and any custom product templates or search modifications. Test the integration on staging, especially if another plugin or theme already replaces WooCommerce search or filtering.

How do product changes reach the search results?

The plugin captures catalogue changes and synchronizes them with the backend through background processing. Changes become searchable after the relevant synchronization and backend processing have completed.

Why is a product update not visible immediately?

Check whether background processing is running and whether synchronization has completed. Publishing an update from WordPress and processing it in the backend are separate steps. Use the plugin’s diagnostics to inspect the current state.

Does SpeedSearch replace my caching plugin?

No. Page caching and dedicated product search address different workloads. Test them together as part of your store’s configuration.

Where can I get help?

Open a topic in the WordPress.org support forum or email wp@tmm.ventures.

Include your WordPress, WooCommerce and SpeedSearch versions, the affected workflow and steps to reproduce the problem. Redact credentials, authentication tokens and private customer information before sharing logs or diagnostics.

1.8.36 2026-10-30

Bugfixes

  • Prevent failed notification requests from creating immediate retry loops with WP Plugins Core 0.1.58; retain bounded retries and interrupted-worker recovery.
  • Avoid repeatedly flushing rewrite rules when the saved shop page ID is a string.
  • Remove dynamic and legacy plugin options during uninstall.

1.8.35 2026-10-22

  • Synchronize feed contents, recovery copies and directory changes before acknowledging publication, retaining pending data when synchronization fails.
  • Repeat persistence checks during crash recovery and lost rename acknowledgements while preserving protocol-1 feed compatibility.
  • Require PHP 8.1 or newer for native file synchronization and expose the durability policy in feed diagnostics.

1.8.34 2026-10-22

  • Remove completed database-feed migration and cleanup helpers while preserving uploads feeds, queues and recovery data.
  • Simplify feed diagnostics and retain a safe upgrade check requiring existing installations to complete cleanup with 1.8.33 first.

1.8.33 2026-10-20

  • Continue pending uploads publication in bounded immediate batches after native scheduler completion, keeping the recurring recovery fallback and preventing duplicate continuation jobs.

1.8.32 2026-10-20

  • Repair historical uploads-feed ordering with verified recovery copies, preserve every record and pending update, and resume protocol-1 publication without regeneration.
  • Continue rejecting duplicate or misplaced feed indexes and identify the offending file, line and index in the error.

1.8.31 2026-10-20

  • Remove the retired database-feed runtime and migration workers after the protocol-1 transition.
  • Remove obsolete snapshot tables and migration data in guarded, resumable batches while retaining active uploads feeds, queues and recovery data.
  • Report cleanup progress in diagnostics and refuse unfinished transitions until the 1.8.30 bridge has completed.

1.8.30 2026-10-20

  • Coalesce ordinary product-save updates into one final snapshot per product per request, with durable retry intent and recovery after interrupted requests.
  • Keep concurrent save requests independent and prevent recovery from acknowledging a save before its later metadata updates finish.
  • Exclude local admission timestamps from feed payloads and hashes to avoid redundant records while preserving real product metadata.
  • Remove deferred feed tickets, cursors and import markers on uninstall; retain pending work on deactivation.

1.8.29 2026-10-19

  • Standardize feed communication on protocol 1 and uploads-based JSONL files. Existing uploads installations retain their feeds without conversion.
  • Migrate existing database feeds in resumable batches, require an exact backend acknowledgement before switching, and retain original data and recovery copies. Requires the compatible Saffy backend deployment first.
  • Coordinate shared uploads writers and recover interrupted publication, regeneration and pending product or taxonomy updates.
  • Remove operational protocol 2 endpoints and snapshot publication controls; expose migration and recovery progress in feed diagnostics.

1.8.28 2026-10-14

  • Keep the uploads feed’s next index and shard hashes in the database, so publishing no longer re-reads and rehashes the whole feed while holding the shared lock. The first publication after upgrading builds this state once.

1.8.27 2026-10-14

  • Defer product and saved-term feed updates to a background worker while the shared feed lock is busy, instead of failing the WooCommerce write that triggered them.

1.8.26 2026-10-13

  • Preserve uploads-based protocol 1 feeds on upgrades from 1.8.20; skip the database-feed import for those installations.
  • Keep existing database-feed installations on protocol 2.
  • Retain file generations and interrupted-import data, with retryable uploads publication through the existing protocol 1 backend endpoints.
  • Report the selected storage mode and skipped data import in feed diagnostics.

1.8.25 2026-10-13

  • Add administrator-only feed diagnostics covering migration checkpoints, protocol acknowledgement, generation and snapshot identities, receipt matching, pending records, retry queues and storage health.
  • Include the report in Show debug data and offer a bounded JSON report, including a link while migration is in progress. Keep credentials and product payloads out of the new report and report unavailable metadata without hiding other progress.

1.8.24 2026-10-13

  • Preserve immutable database feed snapshots across regeneration retries and table swaps.
  • Require a matching backend generation receipt before activating a replacement feed, including empty catalogues.
  • Synchronize the database feed URL and protocol with the backend; retain sources when handoff fails.

1.8.23 2026-10-12

Bugfixes

  • Migrate legacy feeds in bounded, resumable batches during normal requests without loading whole shards into memory.
  • Preserve original files and database recovery copies, resume interrupted imports, and restore feed records left hidden by earlier failed upgrades.
  • Keep migration progress transactional and refuse conflicting pending work instead of silently overwriting it.

1.8.22 2026-10-11

Bugfixes

  • Preserve published feed data and retryable catalogue work across interrupted generation and upgrades.
  • Harden scheduler admission, recovery, cache invalidation, and frontend rendering against failed operations.

1.8.21 2026-09-04

Improvements

  • Make feed generation, pruning, product markup caching, JSON cache settings, and generated script delivery safe across interchangeable load-balanced web nodes by using shared database storage.
  • Preserve existing feed history during upgrades and expose the unchanged JSONL manifest/shard protocol through a database-backed public endpoint.
  • Serialize feed generation transitions and make plugin option reads independent of node-local persistent object-cache state.
  • Remove the legacy product HTML cache (its per-product ID list and cache files) on upgrade, and keep the Advanced diagnostics bounded on large catalogs: they report the cache entry count and pending Action Scheduler count, listing at most 100 pending action IDs, instead of loading every ID.

short_description: Speed up WooCommerce search and filtering. Help shoppers find products with autocomplete, flexible filters and a dedicated search backend.
description:
Help shoppers find the right product faster.

A growing catalogue should give customers more choice without making products harder to find. SpeedSearch brings dedicated product search, autocomplete and flexible filtering to WooCommerce, helping shoppers move from a search or a category to the products that fit.

Search and filtering run on the SpeedSearch backend, reducing the search workload on your WordPress database. Your store gets a product-discovery interface you can configure in WordPress, with background catalogue synchronization to keep it supplied with updates.

Give shoppers more ways to find what they want

  • Search with a head start. Show suggestions and product results as customers type.
  • Turn a large selection into a useful shortlist. Filter by category, tag, price and product attributes such as size, colour or material.
  • Put discovery where it belongs. Place a complete search interface or individual search, filter and results components in your storefront.
  • Keep catalogue changes moving. Synchronize product and taxonomy updates through background processing, with diagnostics to inspect progress.

Give WooCommerce search its own engine

Search and filtering can ask a lot of a store’s database, particularly as its catalogue and filter combinations grow. SpeedSearch synchronizes catalogue data with a dedicated service that finds matching products and processes filters.

This separates those operations from your store’s main WordPress database. It is designed to improve product discovery; actual speed depends on your catalogue, hosting, network, theme and configuration.

Help both focused shoppers and browsers

Some customers arrive with a product in mind. Others start with a category, a budget or a preferred colour. Autocomplete supports the first group; product filters help the second narrow down the options.

Configure the autocomplete presentation and selection behaviour, then choose filters that reflect how people shop your catalogue. Attribute filters use the supported attributes configured on your WooCommerce products.

Fit search into your storefront

Use shortcodes for the full interface or for individual search, filter, category and product-results components. SpeedSearch also includes integrations for Flatsome and its UX Builder.

Adjust the layout and behaviour in WordPress, then check the result with your theme and product templates. You can build around the way your shop presents its products.

See what shoppers are searching for

Search analytics can help you review popular search terms and searches without results. Use those insights to investigate gaps in product naming, catalogue coverage or navigation.

Connect your catalogue and get started

SpeedSearch requires access to the SpeedSearch backend service, store authorization and an initial catalogue synchronization. Installing the plugin alone does not provide service access.

Visit SpeedSearch to learn about the service, review the available plans, or contact wp@tmm.ventures for setup assistance. Paid plans are separate from the plugin download.

External Services

SpeedSearch backend

The plugin connects to the SpeedSearch service to authorize the store, synchronize its catalogue and settings, and process search, autocomplete and filtering requests. The default backend address is https://saffy.speedsearchpro.com; deployments can configure a different address.

Data exchanged includes product and taxonomy information, store settings, search and filter parameters, the store domain, plugin version and service authentication details. During authorization, the plugin also sends the activating administrator’s name and email address as the store contact. Background analytics delivery sends per-product view, add-to-cart and purchase counters.

These requests occur during store connection, catalogue and settings synchronization, search operations and scheduled analytics delivery. Diagnostic and settings-sharing operations also communicate with the backend when used.

Service information: https://speedsearch.io/
For service access, terms and privacy information, contact wp@tmm.ventures.

Tawk.to live chat

SpeedSearch loads Tawk.to’s chat widget in its administration interface to provide support. Loading the widget connects the administrator’s browser to Tawk.to, exposing connection information such as the IP address and browser details. Information entered into the chat is sent to Tawk.to.
